messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: linking problem
parts:
Previously if a Stan program did not use ODEs, it did not matter whether CVODES was linked. But something seems to have changed recently and now rstanarm, which does not currently have any models with ODEs, does not link with the 2.10.0 stuff.

Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :
  unable to load shared object '/tmp/Rtmpm9G9in/Rinst2f355fbfc0d9/rstanarm/libs/rstanarm.so':
  /tmp/Rtmpm9G9in/Rinst2f355fbfc0d9/rstanarm/libs/rstanarm.so: undefined symbol: CVodeSetMaxConvFails
Error: loading failed
Execution halted
ERROR: loading failed

Does anyone have any ideas?

Ben

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] linking problem
parts:
What changed in the meantime is that before these function were part of a templated object. As far as i recall this makes things more header only friendly. However, during the design refactorings this got changed. My guess would be that if we go back to a design where all the cvodes function are part of such an object would solve it ... Or we declare those little functions with "inline" that should do the trick as well if i remember right.

Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] linking problem
parts:
Sebastian's right --- we only run into linker problems if
a template is instantiated (or if we have a non-template function,
which is like an instantiation). Otherwise, the compiler only checks
that it's all well-formed syntactically.

One solution would be to write a custom include for all
the linked packages that don't automatically include CVODES.
Or we could break math.hpp into two pieces, math.hpp and
math-cvodes.hpp.

Managing dependencies is always a burden, which is why I'm so
conservative in wanting to add them to Stan.

- Bob
